title: Lynx: A Unified Foundation Model for Multimodal Radiology — Development and Validation Using Retrospective Clinical Imaging Data
summary: Modern medical imaging produces large amounts of data that are difficult to analyze consistently.The study investigates whether artificial intelligence can learn from routine medical images and reports to support interpretation of medical scans. Retrospective use of fully anonymized imaging data from routine clinical care. A computer model is trained and tested to generate and analyze radiology reports and images without any patient contact or new data collection.

interventions.name: This is a retrospective observational study using anonymized radiological imaging data and associated radiology reports from routine clinical care between 2010 and 2025. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Any patient who received a radiological imaging examination (CT, MRI, PET, X-ray, or US) at the LMU University Hospital between 01-Jan-2010 and 31-Dec-2025
An associated free-text radiology report is available in the RIS
Imaging data is stored in standard DICOM format in the PACS
Exclusion criteria:
Examinations with missing or corrupted imaging data (incomplete DICOM series, unreadable files)
Examinations without an associated radiology report
Examinations where imaging data cannot be successfully converted from DICOM to the required research format (NIfTI for volumetric data, PNG/TIFF for 2D projections)
Examinations flagged for data quality issues during automated quality control (e.g., extreme motion artifacts rendering the study non-diagnostic, truncated field-of-view preventing meaningful analysis)
